# Infusion altar
The infusion altar is a machine that fuses essence and items into new, more powerful ones. The central altar is surrounded by connectable pedestals onto which the required ingredients are placed.
You can examine the altar while wearing thaumaturgic goggles to see the available pedestal placement spots.
## Performing an infusion ritual
- Place a catalyst item on the central altar. - Place the required items on the surrounding pedestals. - Arrange candles and other stabilizers symmetrically around the altar to reduce instability. - Spray the required essence around the altar. - Power the altar and all pedestals from the grid using pipes.
The altar will start drawing in essence, and if all ritual conditions are met, the infusion process will begin.
## Instability While the ritual is running, the altar's instability grows - even with everything set up perfectly, the fusion process is inherently risky by nature. If a ritual condition is broken (not enough essence, an item knocked off a pedestal), instability grows faster.
The higher the instability, the greater the chance of a negative effect triggering each second. In the worst case, negative effects can disrupt the ritual by knocking items off pedestals or damaging the feed pipes. If that happens, you need to quickly restore the ritual's conditions, or cancel it by cutting the power.
An unpowered altar gradually loses instability, but this takes some time, during which negative effects can still occur with a decreasing chance.
## Stabilizers Candles and candelabras placed on the floor around the altar dampen instability growth - but only if arranged symmetrically, in pairs on opposite sides of the altar. An unpaired stabilizer, on the other hand, slightly raises instability.
